title: Coupling Coordination and Multi‐Objective Optimisation of the Human–Water–Land System in Arid Northwest China
content:
ABSTRACT

Sustainable development in arid Northwest China depends on coordinated management of the water resources–socioeconomic–ecological (WSE) system. Understanding the interactions among these subsystems is therefore critical in this water-stressed region. Analysing the interplay among these three systems is thus critical for this water-stressed region. This study establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework for 2000–2023, integrating the entropy weight method, a coupling coordination degree (CCD) model, grey relational analysis, random forest and the NSGA-II multi-objective optimisation algorithm to diagnose their coupling coordination dynamics. The results demonstrate that (1) the coupling coordination index for the arid regions of Northwest China has steadily increased from 0.28 in 2000 to 0.46 in 2023. Core cities such as Urumqi and Karamay have seen particularly significant growth exceeding 0.18. However, the region exhibits pronounced spatial differentiation and uneven development patterns. (2) The ecological water usage ratio and vegetation coverage rate are the most critical drivers for coordinated system development, with grey correlation coefficients of 0.946 and 0.956 respectively, which are significantly higher than the urbanisation rate's 0.811 and GDP growth rate's 0.736. (3) Multi-scenario simulations propose differentiated regulatory strategies, suggesting that economically developed cities under high water stress should prioritise integrated water-socioeconomic management, while ecologically fragile regions are better suited for synergistic water-ecological governance. (4) The study recommends incorporating key indicators, particularly the ecological water allocation ratio, into regional policy evaluation systems to advance precision governance models guided by water-determined development paradigms. This research enhances the understanding of complex human-land system coupling mechanisms in arid regions and provides methodological references for sustainable development studies.
